HOW TO USE THIS FILE (R Markdown basics)
=============================================================
This is an R Markdown notebook (.Rmd) -- plain-text explanation (like
this comment) mixed with "chunks" of R code, delimited by ```{r} ... ```.
Run a chunk with the green play arrow at its top-right or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter
with your cursor in it; run top to bottom the first time through, since
later chunks depend on objects earlier ones create. "Knit" runs the
whole thing and produces one HTML report.

PIPELINE_CORE v3 -- what changed relative to v2
  D. WHERE PEOPLE ACT. Step 6b adds a patch-choice model: at each pick a
     player chooses one of the patches that could still be acted on (the
     logged `landChoices` says which) or chooses to stop. Classes of
     players are now formed from these patch preferences (class_basis =
     "choice"), by recursive splitting so that one class does not swallow
     most people. Needs logs written by tapSquares v3 (landChoices, and a
     STATE for the very first phase); older logs fall back to the v2
     behavior. Variables holding a player number (role = player_reference
     in variableRoles.csv, e.g. cropOwner) become <name>_mine.
  E. New outputs: agent_patch_choice_weights.csv (not yet read by the ABM),
     per-class "where" heat map in the PDF guide.

PIPELINE_CORE v2 -- what changed relative to v1
  A. PERSON IDs. tapSquares v2 writes `PLAYER|number|enteredName|ts` lines.
     Whatever a player typed at HubNet entry IS their ID (`person_id`),
     verbatim (no HHID/name split). The same string in different sessions
     is assumed to be the same person. Per-person fits, clustering and
     class assignment are keyed by `person_id`, not by session-local
     player number. Logs without PLAYER lines fall back to one distinct
     person per session x player (with a warning).
  B. SESSION PARAMETERS AS CANDIDATE TREATMENTS. Scalar numeric / TRUE-FALSE
     parameters named in sessionList.csv are read from each log's header
     (plus a derived `numPlayers`; ignore it with role not_treatment). Those that vary across the pool are
     candidate treatments. Declared ones (variableRoles.csv:
     treatmentCandidate = TRUE or role = session_parameter) and
     auto-detected ones go through the same diagnostics (Step 5a): is there
     enough variation, are they separable from each other, and does
     adding them improve held-out prediction (session-blocked
     cross-validation)? Only those that pass become predictors; the full
     verdict table is written to treatment_report.csv.
  C. Session logs are recognised by content (they contain PHASE/CHOICE/
     STATE/PLAYER lines), not by file name.

PIPELINE_CORE v1 -- reconciled from three copies that had diverged
across games (CropRaider/PES were untouched from the original;
Lantana had added an `excluded_predictors` mechanism and hardened
round/phase into a permanent exclusion; Tiger only differed in a
commented-out toggle). This version is the merge point going forward
-- see CHANGELOG.md in this folder for the full list of what changed
and why. Game-specific behavior belongs in that game's
`variableRoles.csv` (optional, see Step 4a below), never in an edited
copy of this file.

What changed in this version, compared to the one that ran clean
end-to-end on real CropRaider data:
  1. Round/phase (or year, or whatever a game calls its counter) are
     no longer unconditionally barred from being predictors. Some
     games embed real structure in that counter (a multi-year climate
     cycle, a seasonal effect) that a player could plausibly learn
     even with no explicit variable telling them about it. Step 4a
     reads an optional `variableRoles.csv` that can opt a counter
     variable in, and choose how it's encoded (raw numeric, cyclical
     sin/cos for a known period, or categorical) so the model can
     extrapolate to round/phase values it never saw in training
     instead of erroring or silently ignoring a real effect. Default
     behavior with no config file present, or a counter not listed in
     it, is unchanged: excluded, exactly as before.
  2. Land-ownership variables (`ownedBy`, `village`, and similar) get
     explicit handling: a configured sentinel value (e.g. 0) is kept
     as its own real "unassigned" factor level rather than being
     treated as just another number on a continuous scale. This
     matters because ownership in tapSquares games is sometimes
     player-selected, sometimes randomly/game-assigned, and some
     patches can stay unassigned the whole game -- the model needs to
     tell those cases apart, not average over them.
  3. `excluded_predictors` (from the Lantana branch) is kept as-is: a
     simple named-variable dropout list for anything that's a real
     predictor you just don't want in this particular fit.
  4. At the end, if `sessionList.csv` is present in the working
     directory, this notebook now writes `sessionList_ABM.csv` itself
     -- copying every column over and adding the three that point at
     this notebook's own outputs (`agent_behavior_weights.csv`,
     `agent_behavior_reference.csv`, `outcomePlotList.csv`). That
     wiring used to be a manual, error-prone edit; now it's automatic.
     Any other tuning for the ABM run (agent counts, world size, etc.)
     is still a manual edit on top of the generated file.

Honesty check, carried forward: steps 1-3 (parsing, pivoting, the
original single dedup+join+pooled-model path) have run against real
data and work. Steps 7-9 (per-player fits, clustering, per-class
refit, long-format export) were carefully traced by hand but are less
battle-tested -- treat a first error there as a real bug, not caution.
Steps 4a/4b (variable-role handling) are new in this version and have
only been checked against synthetic data, not real session logs yet.
-->

## Settings you may want to edit

```{r settings}
# --- where the session logs are ---
session_dir <- "sample_sessions"      # folder of session logs (.csv or .csv.gz); e.g. "../simulated_scenarios/fine_only"
exclude_game_ids <- 0                 # gameID(s) left out of the analysis, e.g. the practice game (gameID 0); use NULL to keep all

# --- person identity ---
# The string a player typed at entry is their ID, used verbatim. Set TRUE to
# also trim whitespace and ignore case (so "Ana_07" and "ana_07 " match).
normalize_ids <- FALSE

# --- treatment diagnostics (Step 5a) ---
use_autodetected_treatments <- TRUE   # consider session parameters that vary but were not declared
min_sessions_total     <- 8           # fewer sessions than this: no treatment is testable
min_sessions_per_level <- 3           # a treatment level seen in fewer sessions: not testable
max_levels_for_counts  <- 6           # at or below this many distinct values, per-level session counts are checked
max_abs_cor            <- 0.95        # treatments more correlated than this across sessions cannot be separated
cv_folds               <- 5           # session-blocked folds
cv_min_gain            <- 0.001       # held-out log-likelihood gain per decision a treatment must deliver
min_decisions_per_person <- 20        # fewer decisions than this: person is not fitted individually

# --- how weights are estimated and how classes are formed ---
ridge_decay      <- 0.1               # small penalty on all weights (nnet 'decay'). Keeps weights finite when a choice is predicted perfectly from few decisions; 0 = none
n_classes_forced <- NULL              # NULL: choose the number of classes from the data (best silhouette between 2 and max_classes); or a whole number to force it
max_classes      <- 6
class_basis      <- "choice"          # what people are grouped on:
                                      #   "choice": which patches they go for (the patch-choice model, Step 6b)   <- recommended
                                      #   "action":  what they do once on a patch (predicted action probabilities in common situations)
                                      #   "both":    the two together
                                      #   "coefficients": raw per-person action weights (very noisy with few decisions per person)
                                      # If the logs have no landChoices (older games), "choice"/"both" fall back to "action".
n_probes         <- 60                # number of common situations used for "action"
min_class_size   <- 2                 # a split that leaves a class with fewer people than this is not considered
class_split_min_sil <- 0.15           # a split into classes is kept only if its mean silhouette is at least this
class_max_share  <- 0.4               # any class holding more than this share of people is split again if a good split exists

# --- patch-choice model (Step 6b) ---
use_patch_choice       <- TRUE        # model which patch a player goes for next (or whether they stop), alongside what they do there
choice_ridge           <- 5           # penalty on the patch-choice weights (on the standardised scale)
choice_max_alternatives <- 30         # patches considered per pick: the chosen one, "stop", and a random sample of the rest
choice_scenes          <- 60          # common situations used to compare people's patch preferences
min_choice_events_per_person <- 50    # fewer picks than this: person is not fitted individually
use_choice_treatments  <- TRUE        # let session-level treatments shift which patches get picked (Step 6c)
choice_screen_top      <- 8           # treatment x patch-feature terms that pass the screen and go to cross-validation
choice_screen_min_t    <- 2           # a term must show at least this session-level t-statistic to pass the screen
choice_cv_max_events   <- 12000       # picks used in the cross-validation (a random subset, to keep it fast)

# --- hand-off to the ABM (last chunk) ---
promote_to_abm <- TRUE                # TRUE: copy the outputs into the ABM folder and add the treatment widgets to the ABM interface
abm_dir        <- "../abm"            # where the ABM folder is, relative to this notebook (the usual game layout)

# --- synthesis guide (Step 11) ---
make_pdf_report <- TRUE               # write a PDF guide to the dataset and the fitted model
report_file     <- "dataset_guide.pdf"
loading_clip    <- 10                 # heat-map colours are clipped at +/- this weight (numbers in cells are not)
```

## Point this at your session log(s)

```{r path}
# Default: every .csv in sample_sessions/. Swap to a single file (or a
# short explicit vector) once you're working with one real session:
#   log_paths <- "real_session.csv"
log_paths <- list.files(session_dir, pattern = "\\.csv(\\.gz)?$", full.names = TRUE)

# Anything else dropped in this folder (MANIFEST.csv, a README export, ...)
# isn't a session log. Decide by content, not by name: a session log has
# lines starting with PHASE|, CHOICE|, STATE| or PLAYER|.
is_session_log <- function(path) {
  ln <- tryCatch(read_lines(path), error = function(e) character(0))
  any(str_detect(ln, "^(PHASE|CHOICE|STATE|PLAYER)\\|"))
}
log_paths <- log_paths[map_lgl(log_paths, is_session_log)]

if (length(log_paths) == 0) {
  stop("log_paths is empty -- check your working directory (", getwd(), ").")
}
missing_files <- log_paths[!file.exists(log_paths)]
if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop("Can't find: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "), " (working directory: ", getwd(), "). ",
       "Check the path, and Session > Set Working Directory in RStudio if needed.")
}

log_paths
```

## Step 1: parse one file into tagged tables

```{r parse-function}
tag_schema <- list(
  STATE             = c("round", "phase", "x", "y", "name", "value"),
  CHOICE            = c("round", "phase", "player", "x", "y", "actionID", "timestamp"),
  CONFIRM           = c("round", "phase", "player", "timestamp"),
  VILLAGE           = c("round", "phase", "player", "x", "y", "status", "timestamp"),
  VILLAGECONFIRMED  = c("village", "x", "y", "status", "timestamp"),
  PRIVATE           = c("round", "phase", "player", "x", "y", "status", "timestamp"),
  PRIVATECONFIRMED  = c("player", "x", "y", "status", "timestamp"),
  SCORE             = c("round", "phase", "player", "currentScore", "totalScore", "resources"),
  PHASE             = c("label", "timestamp"),
  PLAYER            = c("player", "name", "timestamp"),  # v2: what each player typed at entry = their ID
  OVERRIDE          = c("variable", "value", "timestamp") # v2 ABM: a setting changed by a slider after the session row was loaded
)

build_table <- function(split_lines, tags_found, tag, session_id) {
  cols <- tag_schema[[tag]]
  rows <- split_lines[tags_found == tag]
  rows <- map(rows, ~ .x[-1])
  good <- map_lgl(rows, ~ length(.x) == length(cols))
  if (any(!good)) {
    warning(sprintf("%s (%s): dropped %d malformed line(s) with the wrong field count",
                     tag, session_id, sum(!good)))
  }
  rows <- rows[good]
  if (length(rows) == 0) {
    empty <- setNames(rep(list(character(0)), length(cols)), cols)   # one empty column per field
    df <- tibble::as_tibble(empty)
  } else {
    df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(df) <- cols
    df <- tibble::as_tibble(df)
  }
  df$session_id <- session_id
  df
}

# Header lines look like `key: value` (no "|"). Keep the FIRST occurrence of
# each key whose value is a scalar number or true/false. A list-valued numeric
# parameter (e.g. pRain "0.1 0.3 1") is kept only as its mean, named
# <key>_mean, and flagged so the diagnostics can say it is not ABM-evaluable.
parse_header_params <- function(raw_lines, tags_found, session_id) {
  is_hdr <- !(tags_found %in% names(tag_schema)) & str_detect(raw_lines, "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.?-]*: ")
  hl <- raw_lines[is_hdr]
  if (length(hl) == 0) return(tibble(session_id = character(), variable = character(), value = character(), derived = logical()))
  m <- str_match(hl, "^([^:]+): (.*)$")
  h <- tibble(variable = m[, 2], value = str_trim(m[, 3])) %>% filter(!duplicated(variable))
  num_re  <- "^-?[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$"
  is_bool   <- tolower(h$value) %in% c("true", "false")
  is_num    <- str_detect(h$value, num_re)
  # a short single-token string (no spaces) is a categorical setting, e.g. mode: fence
  is_str    <- !is_bool & !is_num & str_detect(h$value, "^[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+$")
  is_scalar <- is_bool | is_num | is_str
  is_list   <- !is_scalar & str_detect(h$value, paste0("^", "-?[0-9.eE+-]+( +-?[0-9.eE+-]+)+$"))
  scal <- h[is_scalar, ] %>%
    mutate(value = if_else(tolower(value) %in% c("true", "false"), tolower(value), value), derived = FALSE)
  lst  <- h[is_list, ] %>%
    mutate(value = map_chr(value, ~ as.character(mean(as.numeric(str_split(.x, " +")[[1]]), na.rm = TRUE))),
           variable = paste0(variable, "_mean"), derived = TRUE)
  out <- bind_rows(scal, lst) %>% mutate(session_id = session_id) %>% select(session_id, variable, value, derived)
  out
}

# An OVERRIDE line (ABM sliders) replaces the header value of the same setting,
# or adds it if the header did not carry it. Last override wins.
apply_overrides <- function(header, overrides) {
  if (nrow(overrides) == 0) return(header)
  ov <- overrides %>%
    mutate(value = str_trim(value), value = if_else(tolower(value) %in% c("true", "false"), tolower(value), value)) %>%
    group_by(variable) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(ov))) {
    hit <- header$variable == ov$variable[i]
    if (any(hit)) header$value[hit] <- ov$value[i]
    else header <- bind_rows(header, tibble(session_id = ov$session_id[i], variable = ov$variable[i],
                                           value = ov$value[i], derived = FALSE))
  }
  header
}

parse_one_log <- function(path) {
  session_id <- sub("\\.csv(\\.gz)?$", "", basename(path))
  raw_lines <- read_lines(path)
  split_lines <- str_split(raw_lines, fixed("|"))
  tags_found  <- map_chr(split_lines, ~ .x[1])

  list(
    state   = build_table(split_lines, tags_found, "STATE", session_id),
    choice  = build_table(split_lines, tags_found, "CHOICE", session_id),
    confirm = build_table(split_lines, tags_found, "CONFIRM", session_id),
    score   = build_table(split_lines, tags_found, "SCORE", session_id),
    roster  = build_table(split_lines, tags_found, "PLAYER", session_id),
    header  = apply_overrides(parse_header_params(raw_lines, tags_found, session_id),
                              build_table(split_lines, tags_found, "OVERRIDE", session_id))
  )
}
```

## Step 2: parse every file and combine

```{r parse-all}
parsed_sessions <- map(log_paths, parse_one_log)
if (length(exclude_game_ids) > 0) {
  is_excluded <- map_lgl(parsed_sessions, function(ps) {
    g <- ps$header$value[ps$header$variable == "gameID"]
    length(g) > 0 && g[1] %in% as.character(exclude_game_ids)
  })
  if (any(is_excluded)) message("Left out ", sum(is_excluded), " log(s) with gameID in {", paste(exclude_game_ids, collapse = ", "), "} (practice games). Set exclude_game_ids <- NULL to keep them.")
  log_paths <- log_paths[!is_excluded]; parsed_sessions <- parsed_sessions[!is_excluded]
}

state_long <- map(parsed_sessions, "state")   %>% bind_rows()
choice     <- map(parsed_sessions, "choice")  %>% bind_rows()
confirm    <- map(parsed_sessions, "confirm") %>% bind_rows()
score      <- map(parsed_sessions, "score")   %>% bind_rows()

to_num <- function(df, cols) df %>% mutate(across(all_of(cols), as.numeric))

state_long <- to_num(state_long, c("round", "phase", "x", "y"))
choice     <- to_num(choice, c("round", "phase", "player", "x", "y", "actionID"))
score      <- to_num(score, c("round", "phase", "player", "currentScore", "totalScore", "resources"))

cat("sessions:", n_distinct(choice$session_id), "\n")
cat("state rows:", nrow(state_long), " choice rows:", nrow(choice),
    " confirm rows:", nrow(confirm), " score rows:", nrow(score), "\n")

choice %>% group_by(session_id) %>% summarise(n_players = n_distinct(player))
```

## Step 2a: who is who (person IDs) and what each session's settings were

```{r roster}
roster <- map(parsed_sessions, "roster") %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(player = as.numeric(player))

# Every (session, player number) that acted gets a person_id: the entered
# string verbatim; if a log has no PLAYER line for that player, a
# session-local placeholder (a distinct "person" that cannot be linked
# to any other session).
players_seen <- choice %>% distinct(session_id, player)
person_map <- players_seen %>%
  left_join(roster %>% select(session_id, player, entered = name), by = c("session_id", "player")) %>%
  mutate(person_id = if_else(is.na(entered) | entered == "", paste0(session_id, "#", player), entered))

if (normalize_ids) {
  person_map <- person_map %>% mutate(person_id = if_else(is.na(entered), person_id, tolower(str_trim(person_id))))
}

no_roster <- person_map %>% filter(is.na(entered) | entered == "")
if (nrow(no_roster) > 0) {
  warning(n_distinct(no_roster$session_id), " session(s) have no PLAYER line for ", nrow(no_roster),
          " player(s): each is treated as a separate person (cannot be linked across sessions).")
}

# Two players in ONE session with the same ID would merge two people; make them distinct and say so.
dups <- person_map %>% count(session_id, person_id) %>% filter(n > 1)
if (nrow(dups) > 0) {
  warning("Duplicate person IDs within a session: ", paste(unique(dups$person_id), collapse = ", "),
          " -- suffixed with ~player number to keep them separate.")
  person_map <- person_map %>%
    group_by(session_id, person_id) %>%
    mutate(person_id = if_else(n() > 1, paste0(person_id, "~", player), person_id)) %>%
    ungroup()
}
person_map <- person_map %>% select(session_id, player, person_id)

person_summary <- person_map %>% count(person_id, name = "n_sessions")
cat("distinct persons:", nrow(person_summary), " | persons seen in 2+ sessions:", sum(person_summary$n_sessions > 1), "\n")

# Session settings from the logs' headers. Only variables that are columns of
# sessionList.csv are candidates (when that file is present).
header_all <- map(parsed_sessions, "header") %>% bind_rows()
if (file.exists("sessionList.csv")) {
  sl_cols <- names(read_csv("sessionList.csv", n_max = 0, show_col_types = FALSE))
  sl_cols <- c(sl_cols, paste0(sl_cols, "_mean"))
  header_all <- header_all %>% filter(variable %in% sl_cols)
}
list_derived <- unique(header_all$variable[header_all$derived])

coerce_param <- function(x) {
  if (all(x %in% c("true", "false", NA))) return(x == "true")
  n <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  if (!any(is.na(n) & !is.na(x))) return(n)
  x   # categorical (text) setting
}
session_params <- header_all %>%
  select(session_id, variable, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(across(-session_id, coerce_param))

# Derived numPlayers (how many people joined) is offered as a candidate like any
# other setting. If it is not a manipulation in your game, give it the role
# not_treatment in variableRoles.csv and it is ignored.
np <- person_map %>% count(session_id, name = "numPlayers")
if (!"numPlayers" %in% names(session_params)) {
  session_params <- session_params %>% full_join(np, by = "session_id")
}
session_params <- session_params %>% filter(session_id %in% unique(choice$session_id))

cat("session settings read from log headers:", paste(setdiff(names(session_params), "session_id"), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Step 3: reshape state from long to wide

```{r pivot-state}
state_wide <- state_long %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(session_id, round, phase, x, y), names_from = name, values_from = value)

smart_coerce <- function(x) {
  if (all(x %in% c("true", "false", NA))) return(x == "true")
  numeric_try <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  if (!any(is.na(numeric_try) & !is.na(x))) return(numeric_try)
  x  # leave as character -- e.g. playerHarvestRound's "[1 2 3]" list literal
}

state_wide <- state_wide %>% mutate(across(-c(session_id, round, phase, x, y), smart_coerce))

list_shaped <- names(state_wide)[map_lgl(state_wide, ~ is.character(.x) && any(str_detect(.x, fixed("[")), na.rm = TRUE))]
if (length(list_shaped) > 0) {
  message("List-shaped columns left as text, not used as predictors below: ",
          paste(list_shaped, collapse = ", "))
}
```

## Step 4: collapse taps into real decisions, without losing the taps themselves

One row per action, per the earlier reasoning (a turn can span several
patches, so one-row-per-turn doesn't fit a rectangular dataset). But
`update-current-choice` cycles through options each time a player taps
the *same* patch again, so only the last tap per patch is the real
decision -- the earlier ones are menu-browsing, not separate choices.

The count is kept as `n_taps_patch` (how many times this specific
patch was retapped) and `n_taps_turn` (how many total taps happened
across every patch this player touched that round/phase). Read these
two differently: `n_taps_turn` is a reasonable candidate *predictor*
-- it describes how much deliberation a player brought to the whole
turn, independent of which specific action they ended up taking
anywhere in it. `n_taps_patch` is murkier as a predictor of the action
chosen *on that same patch*, since the cycling order itself is fixed
by the game code. Left in as a candidate either way -- just worth
treating with more suspicion than the state variables.

```{r dedup-choice}
cat("choice rows before collapsing cycling taps:", nrow(choice), "\n")

choice <- choice %>%
  group_by(session_id, round, phase, player, x, y) %>%
  mutate(n_taps_patch = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(session_id, round, phase, player) %>%
  mutate(n_taps_turn = n()) %>%
  ungroup()

choice_real <- choice %>%
  group_by(session_id, round, phase, player, x, y) %>%
  slice_tail(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("choice rows after collapsing to real decisions:", nrow(choice_real), "\n")

# tapSquares uses -99 as the sentinel for "explicitly chose nothing here."
# TRUE keeps it as a real outcome level (modeling "did they act at all,
# and on what" together); FALSE models only the choice of *which* action,
# conditional on having taken one. Either is defensible -- flip this and
# re-run rather than picking one silently.
include_no_action_choice <- TRUE
if (!include_no_action_choice) {
  choice_real <- choice_real %>% filter(actionID != -99)
  cat("choice rows after dropping 'no action' (-99):", nrow(choice_real), "\n")
}
```

## Step 4a: load this game's variable-roles config (optional)

`variableRoles.csv` is per-game, optional, and lives alongside the
session logs. It tells this notebook how to treat three kinds of
variable that need more than "is it numeric or logical":

- **counters** (`round`, `phase`, `year`, or whatever a game calls its
  turn/cycle number). Default (not listed, or no config file at all)
  is `exclude` -- identical to every prior version of this notebook.
  List one here with `encoding = numeric` to test it as a plain linear
  predictor, or `encoding = cyclical` with a `period` to test it as a
  repeating cycle (encoded as sin/cos pairs so the model can
  extrapolate to a round number it never saw in training, rather than
  needing every value seen during fitting).
- **ownership** (`ownedBy`, `village`, or similar). `role =
  ownership_individual`/`ownership_group` treats the variable as a
  category (its sentinel value, e.g. 0 for unassigned, becomes its own
  distinct level) rather than a number the model averages over.
  `unassignedValue` is documentation for humans reading the config --
  not consumed by this notebook -- so the raw value stays the level
  text, matching what the ABM generator reads back from the patch.
- **treatment candidates**: `treatmentCandidate = TRUE` doesn't change
  modeling at all -- it's a flag carried through to the export/notes
  so an ABM user knows which variables are the ones worth sweeping.

A blank template with all of this documented lives at
`variableRoles_TEMPLATE.csv` in pipeline_core.

```{r load-variable-roles}
role_schema <- c("variable", "role", "encoding", "period", "unassignedValue", "treatmentCandidate", "notes")

if (file.exists("variableRoles.csv")) {
  variable_roles <- read_csv("variableRoles.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  missing_cols <- setdiff(role_schema, names(variable_roles))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop("variableRoles.csv is missing column(s): ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  cat("Loaded variableRoles.csv:", nrow(variable_roles), "variable(s) configured.\n")
} else {
  variable_roles <- tibble(variable = character(), role = character(), encoding = character(),
                            period = character(), unassignedValue = character(),
                            treatmentCandidate = character(), notes = character())
  message("No variableRoles.csv found -- using defaults (round/phase excluded, everything else auto-detected).")
}

variable_roles
```

## Step 4b: apply counter and ownership encodings to the wide state table

```{r apply-variable-roles}
counter_defaults <- c("round", "phase")  # always excluded unless explicitly overridden below

# Cyclical counters: replace the raw column with sin/cos pairs.
cyclical_rows <- variable_roles %>% filter(role == "counter", encoding == "cyclical")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(cyclical_rows))) {
  v <- cyclical_rows$variable[i]
  p <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cyclical_rows$period[i]))
  if (v %in% names(state_wide) && !is.na(p) && p > 0) {
    state_wide[[paste0(v, "_sin")]] <- sin(2 * pi * state_wide[[v]] / p)
    state_wide[[paste0(v, "_cos")]] <- cos(2 * pi * state_wide[[v]] / p)
    message(v, ": encoded as cyclical (period = ", p, ") -> ", v, "_sin, ", v, "_cos")
  } else if (v %in% names(state_wide)) {
    warning(v, ": role=counter, encoding=cyclical but no valid 'period' given -- left out of the model.")
  }
}

# Numeric counters: leave the raw column in place, just don't structurally exclude it below.
numeric_counter_vars <- variable_roles %>% filter(role == "counter", encoding == "numeric") %>% pull(variable)

# Categorical counters (rare -- won't extrapolate to an unseen round/phase value,
# only use this if you specifically want "round 3" treated as a distinct category).
categorical_counter_vars <- variable_roles %>% filter(role == "counter", encoding == "categorical") %>% pull(variable)
for (v in categorical_counter_vars) {
  if (v %in% names(state_wide)) state_wide[[v]] <- factor(state_wide[[v]])
}

# Ownership variables: treated as a category (factor), not a number on a
# continuous scale, so the sentinel (e.g. 0 = unassigned) is just another
# distinct level rather than something the model averages toward. The raw
# value is kept AS the level text (e.g. "0", "1", "2") rather than
# relabeled to a word like "unassigned" -- R's dummy-coded coefficient
# name is then <varname><rawvalue> (e.g. "village0"), which the ABM
# generator's get-feature-value resolves by reading that same patch
# variable's current value back as text. Relabeling to a word here would
# require the ABM side to separately know the unassignedValue mapping
# from variableRoles.csv just to reverse it -- unnecessary coupling for
# no modeling benefit, since factor() already gives 0 its own level
# either way. unassignedValue in variableRoles.csv is documentation for
# humans reading the config, not consumed here.
ownership_rows <- variable_roles %>% filter(role %in% c("ownership_individual", "ownership_group"))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ownership_rows))) {
  v <- ownership_rows$variable[i]
  if (v %in% names(state_wide)) {
    state_wide[[v]] <- factor(as.character(state_wide[[v]]))
    message(v, ": encoded as ownership factor (levels: ",
            paste(levels(state_wide[[v]]), collapse = ", "), ")")
  }
}

# round/phase stay excluded from the id-column list below UNLESS they were
# given a non-"exclude" encoding above (numeric, cyclical, or categorical).
counter_included <- variable_roles %>%
  filter(role == "counter", encoding %in% c("numeric", "cyclical", "categorical")) %>%
  pull(variable)
counters_to_exclude <- setdiff(counter_defaults, counter_included)

cat("Counters excluded from modeling:", paste(counters_to_exclude, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (length(counter_included) > 0) cat("Counters included (see encoding above):", paste(counter_included, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Step 5: build one row per decision

```{r model-data}
model_data <- choice_real %>%
  left_join(person_map, by = c("session_id", "player")) %>%
  left_join(state_wide, by = c("session_id", "round", "phase", "x", "y")) %>%
  left_join(score, by = c("session_id", "round", "phase", "player"))

# Session-level settings join in last. A setting whose name collides with a
# patch/score variable is dropped from treatment consideration (it would be
# ambiguous which one the model, and later the ABM, means).
sp_collide <- intersect(setdiff(names(session_params), "session_id"), names(model_data))
if (length(sp_collide) > 0) {
  message("Session settings dropped (name collides with a state/score variable): ", paste(sp_collide, collapse = ", "))
  session_params <- session_params %>% select(-all_of(sp_collide))
}
session_param_cols <- setdiff(names(session_params), "session_id")
model_data <- model_data %>% left_join(session_params, by = "session_id") %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(session_param_cols), ~ if (is.character(.x)) factor(.x) else .x))

# Variables that hold a PLAYER NUMBER (role = player_reference in variableRoles.csv, e.g. cropOwner)
# are meaningless as raw numbers; what matters is whether the value is the acting player.
# Replace each by <name>_mine (1 if it equals the player making the choice, else 0).
# The ABM computes the same quantity from the agent's own number.
ref_vars <- intersect(variable_roles$variable[variable_roles$role == "player_reference"], names(model_data))
for (v in ref_vars) {
  model_data[[paste0(v, "_mine")]] <- as.numeric(as.numeric(as.character(model_data[[v]])) == model_data$player)
  model_data[[paste0(v, "_mine")]][is.na(model_data[[paste0(v, "_mine")]])] <- 0
}
if (length(ref_vars) > 0) message("player_reference variables replaced by <name>_mine: ", paste(ref_vars, collapse = ", "))

# Always-bookkeeping columns: join keys / identifiers, never candidate
# predictors regardless of configuration. round/phase are handled
# separately just above -- excluded by default, includable via
# variableRoles.csv -- since unlike these, a game *can* meaningfully
# encode real state in its counter.
id_cols <- c("session_id", "player", "person_id", "x", "y", "actionID", "timestamp")
id_cols <- union(id_cols, counters_to_exclude)

predictor_cols <- setdiff(names(model_data), id_cols)
predictor_cols <- predictor_cols[map_lgl(model_data[predictor_cols],
                                          ~ is.numeric(.x) || is.logical(.x) || is.factor(.x))]

## Choose which real predictors the choice model may use
##
## `session_id`, `player`, `x`, `y`, `actionID`, and `timestamp` are
## never candidates -- they're bookkeeping from the log format itself
## (join keys and identifiers), not variables that exist anywhere in
## the actual game/ABM. round/phase are excluded by the same logic
## UNLESS variableRoles.csv opted them in (Step 4a/4b) -- see that
## section for why a game might want to.
##
## What *does* belong in excluded_predictors below: any predictor
## that's real (a patches-own variable that's actually in this game,
## or a score-derived feature like `resources`) but that you know
## isn't meaningful for this analysis and want dropped without
## touching the data or the model-fitting code. Empty by default.
excluded_predictors <- ref_vars   # raw player-number columns; their <name>_mine versions are used instead

predictor_cols <- setdiff(predictor_cols, excluded_predictors)

# Session-level settings are NOT part of the base predictor set; Step 5a
# decides which (if any) of them earn a place.
predictor_cols <- setdiff(predictor_cols, session_param_cols)
predictor_cols_base <- predictor_cols

cat("Excluded from the choice model by name (edit excluded_predictors above to add any):\n",
    if (length(excluded_predictors) == 0) "(none)" else paste(excluded_predictors, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# tapSquares names boolean patches-own variables with a trailing "?"
# (water?, cropped?, ...) -- not valid bare terms in an R formula, so
# every predictor gets backtick-wrapped regardless of whether it needs
# it. Works the same for factor columns (ownership, categorical
# counters) as for numeric/logical ones.
predictor_terms <- paste0("`", predictor_cols, "`")

cat("Predictors used (includes n_taps_patch, n_taps_turn):\n", paste(predictor_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Coefficients from separately-fit models are only comparable if every
# model uses the same reference/baseline outcome category. Fix one
# explicitly and reuse it for every fit below (pooled, per-player,
# per-class) rather than letting each fit pick its own default.
#
# The reference category MUST be -99 ("do nothing") whenever it's present
# in the data, not just "whichever action happens to be most common."
# A multinomial logit's reference level always scores exactly 0 -- no
# fitted coefficients, no dependence on state at all, by construction --
# and the ABM (choose-actions-for-agent, tapSquares_ABM_generator.nlogox)
# picks every action by comparing its fitted score against -99's fitted
# score (the margin over "doing nothing"). That comparison is only
# mathematically sound when -99 itself is the reference: then every real
# action's score directly IS its own log-odds relative to doing nothing,
# and "margin > 0" means exactly what it's supposed to. Pick anything
# else as reference and that ONE action instead gets pinned to a flat,
# state-independent 0 score forever, while -99 gets real (often
# comparatively favorable) fitted coefficients -- so the reference action
# ends up silently, permanently excluded from every ABM agent's choices,
# for a reason that has nothing to do with real behavior, just an
# artifact of which action happened to get picked as the baseline.
# Confirmed live: Crouching Tiger's synthetic training data (near-uniform
# random action choice, no real signal) happened to make actionID 4
# (buildFence) the most-frequent action by sampling noise alone -- it
# became the reference, and fence-building was never chosen by any ABM
# agent afterward, regardless of session/round/patch state.
if (-99 %in% model_data$actionID) {
  reference_action <- -99
} else {
  # -99 never appears in this session's data (every player acted every
  # turn) -- fall back to the most frequent real action, same as before.
  reference_action <- model_data %>% count(actionID, sort = TRUE) %>% slice(1) %>% pull(actionID)
  message("Note: -99 (\"do nothing\") never appears in this session's data -- ",
          "falling back to the most frequent action (", reference_action,
          ") as the reference category instead.")
}
model_data <- model_data %>% mutate(actionID_f = relevel(factor(actionID), ref = as.character(reference_action)))
cat("Reference category for all model fits below: actionID =", reference_action, "\n")

make_form <- function(cols) as.formula(paste("actionID_f ~", paste0("`", cols, "`", collapse = " + ")))
form_base <- make_form(predictor_cols_base)

# A predictor that does not vary in the rows a given fit uses (a one-level
# factor such as `village` when every patch logs 0, a constant numeric, a
# column that is all NA) cannot be estimated and makes multinom() stop with
# "contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels". This
# happens in the pooled data, and far more often in subsets (one person,
# one class, one cross-validation fold). So every fit goes through fit_mn(),
# which first drops predictors that do not vary in ITS data, repeating
# until stable because dropping a column can change which rows are complete.
varying_cols <- function(data, cols) {
  cols <- cols[map_lgl(cols, ~ n_distinct(data[[.x]][!is.na(data[[.x]])]) > 1)]
  repeat {
    d <- data[complete.cases(data[, c("actionID_f", cols), drop = FALSE]), , drop = FALSE]
    keep <- cols[map_lgl(cols, ~ n_distinct(d[[.x]]) > 1)]
    if (length(keep) == length(cols)) break
    cols <- keep
  }
  cols
}
fit_mn <- function(cols, data, ...) {
  keep <- varying_cols(data, cols)
  dropped <- setdiff(cols, keep)
  if (length(dropped) > 0) message("Not estimable in this fit (no variation), left out: ", paste(dropped, collapse = ", "))
  data <- droplevels(data[complete.cases(data[, c("actionID_f", keep), drop = FALSE]), , drop = FALSE])
  frm <- if (length(keep) == 0) as.formula("actionID_f ~ 1") else make_form(keep)
  # do.call (not a plain call): multinom() stores its call and summary()/vcov()
  # re-evaluate it later, so the formula and data must be values in the call,
  # not names that only exist inside this function.
  do.call(multinom, c(list(formula = frm, data = data, trace = FALSE, MaxNWts = 50000, decay = ridge_decay), list(...)))
}
form <- form_base   # Step 5a extends this with any treatments that pass
can_fit_model <- n_distinct(model_data$actionID) >= 2
if (!can_fit_model) {
  message("Only one action type appears in this data -- can't fit a choice model yet.")
}

model_data
```


## Step 5a: which session settings can be treated as treatments?

Every scalar session setting that **varies across the pool of logs** is a
candidate treatment. Nothing is assumed about which ones matter: ones you
declared (`variableRoles.csv`: `treatmentCandidate = TRUE`, or `role =
session_parameter`) and ones the notebook found on its own are put through
the same checks, in this order:

1. **Enough variation?** Not constant; at least `min_sessions_total`
   sessions; each level (when there are few levels) seen in at least
   `min_sessions_per_level` sessions.
2. **Separable?** Settings that move together across sessions (|cor| above
   `max_abs_cor`, or linearly dependent) cannot be told apart; the
   declared one is kept, the other is reported as aliased.
3. **Does it help?** Session-blocked cross-validation: sessions are split
   into folds, and a treatment must raise the held-out log-likelihood per
   decision by at least `cv_min_gain` over the state-only model, and the
   accepted set together must too. This is what stops a treatment that
   merely fits session-level noise from being exported as a "weight."

Only treatments passing all three become predictors. Everything else
(including why) is in `treatment_report.csv`. A treatment that fails is not
shown to be irrelevant, only that this pool cannot demonstrate an effect.
Settings enter as additive terms; effects that exist only in combination
with a state (for example a fine that matters only on protected land) are
not modeled yet.

```{r treatment-diagnostics}
declared_treatments <- variable_roles %>%
  filter(toupper(treatmentCandidate) %in% c("TRUE", "T", "YES", "1") | role == "session_parameter") %>%
  pull(variable)
not_treatments <- variable_roles %>% filter(role == "not_treatment") %>% pull(variable)

cand <- setdiff(session_param_cols, not_treatments)
if (!use_autodetected_treatments) cand <- intersect(cand, declared_treatments)
cand <- c(intersect(declared_treatments, cand), setdiff(cand, declared_treatments))  # declared first
missing_declared <- setdiff(declared_treatments, session_param_cols)
if (length(missing_declared) > 0) {
  message("Declared as treatment but not found as a scalar setting in the log headers: ",
          paste(missing_declared, collapse = ", "))
}

sp <- session_params %>% filter(session_id %in% unique(model_data$session_id))
n_sess <- nrow(sp)

diag_rows <- lapply(cand, function(v) {
  x <- sp[[v]]
  nd <- length(unique(x[!is.na(x)]))
  min_lvl <- if (nd <= max_levels_for_counts && nd > 0) min(table(x)) else NA_integer_
  verdict <- "adequate"; why <- character(0)
  is_cat <- is.character(x)
  if (nd < 2) {
    verdict <- "not testable"; why <- "constant across all sessions"
  } else if (is_cat && nd > max_levels_for_counts) {
    verdict <- "not testable"; why <- sprintf("text setting with %d distinct values (looks like free text or a path, not a small set of conditions)", nd)
  } else {
    if (n_sess < min_sessions_total) {
      verdict <- "not testable"; why <- c(why, sprintf("only %d sessions (need %d)", n_sess, min_sessions_total))
    }
    if (!is.na(min_lvl) && min_lvl < min_sessions_per_level) {
      verdict <- "not testable"; why <- c(why, sprintf("a level occurs in only %d session(s) (need %d)", min_lvl, min_sessions_per_level))
    }
    if (verdict != "not testable" && nd == 2 && !is_cat) {
      verdict <- "limited"; why <- c(why, "two levels only: direction testable, shape is not")
    }
  }
  xn <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  if (nd >= 2 && nd == n_sess && !any(is.na(xn)) && all(xn == round(xn))) {
    # a different whole number in every session is a label (sessionID, gameID), not a manipulation
    verdict <- "not testable"; why <- c(why, "a different integer in every session: looks like an identifier")
  }
  if (v %in% list_derived) why <- c(why, "mean of a list-valued setting; the ABM cannot evaluate this name")
  tibble(variable = v,
         source = if (v %in% declared_treatments) "declared" else "auto-detected",
         n_sessions = n_sess, n_distinct = nd,
         min_value = if (is_cat) NA_real_ else suppressWarnings(min(as.numeric(x), na.rm = TRUE)),
         max_value = if (is_cat) NA_real_ else suppressWarnings(max(as.numeric(x), na.rm = TRUE)),
         min_sessions_per_level = min_lvl,
         variation_verdict = verdict, notes = paste(why, collapse = "; "),
         abm_evaluable = !(v %in% list_derived),
         type = if (is.logical(x)) "logical" else if (is_cat) "categorical" else "numeric",
         levels = if (is_cat) paste(sort(unique(x)), collapse = ";") else NA_character_,
         integer_valued = is.numeric(x) && !anyNA(x) && all(x == round(x)))
})
treatment_diag <- if (length(diag_rows) > 0) bind_rows(diag_rows) else
  tibble(variable = character(), source = character(), n_sessions = integer(), n_distinct = integer(),
         min_value = numeric(), max_value = numeric(), min_sessions_per_level = integer(),
         variation_verdict = character(), notes = character(), abm_evaluable = logical(),
         type = character(), levels = character(), integer_valued = logical())

# --- separability (aliasing) among the testable ones ---
eligible <- treatment_diag %>% filter(variation_verdict != "not testable", abm_evaluable) %>% pull(variable)
alias_dropped <- character(0)
# numeric design columns for a setting: itself, or dummy columns for a categorical one
design_block <- function(v) {
  x <- sp[[v]]
  if (is.character(x)) {
    lv <- sort(unique(x))[-1]
    matrix(sapply(lv, function(l) as.numeric(x == l)), nrow = length(x))
  } else matrix(as.numeric(x), ncol = 1)
}
if (length(eligible) > 1) {
  blocks <- setNames(lapply(eligible, design_block), eligible)
  for (i in seq_along(eligible)[-1]) {
    for (j in seq_len(i - 1)) {
      vi <- eligible[i]; vj <- eligible[j]
      if (vi %in% alias_dropped || vj %in% alias_dropped) next
      cc <- suppressWarnings(abs(cor(blocks[[vi]], blocks[[vj]])))
      r <- suppressWarnings(max(cc, na.rm = TRUE))
      if (is.finite(r) && r > max_abs_cor) alias_dropped <- c(alias_dropped, vi)
    }
  }
  kept <- setdiff(eligible, alias_dropped)
  if (length(kept) > 1) {
    Xk <- cbind(1, do.call(cbind, blocks[kept]))
    owner <- c("(Intercept)", rep(kept, map_int(blocks[kept], ncol)))
    q <- qr(Xk)
    if (q$rank < ncol(Xk)) {
      alias_dropped <- c(alias_dropped, unique(owner[q$pivot[seq_len(ncol(Xk)) > q$rank]]))
    }
  }
}
if (length(alias_dropped) > 0) {
  treatment_diag <- treatment_diag %>%
    mutate(notes = if_else(variable %in% alias_dropped,
                           paste0(notes, if_else(notes == "", "", "; "), "moves together with another setting across sessions: effects cannot be separated"),
                           notes),
           variation_verdict = if_else(variable %in% alias_dropped, "not testable", variation_verdict))
  eligible <- setdiff(eligible, alias_dropped)
}

# --- does it improve held-out prediction? (folds are whole sessions) ---
cv_ll <- function(cols, data, folds) {
  per_row <- lapply(sort(unique(folds)), function(f) {
    tr <- data[folds != f, ]; te <- data[folds == f, ]
    tr$actionID_f <- droplevels(tr$actionID_f)
    if (nlevels(tr$actionID_f) < 2) return(NA_real_)
    m <- tryCatch(fit_mn(cols, tr, maxit = 100), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(m)) return(NA_real_)
    p <- tryCatch(predict(m, newdata = te, type = "probs"), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(p)) return(NA_real_)
    if (is.null(dim(p))) { p <- cbind(1 - p, p); colnames(p) <- m$lev }
    idx <- match(as.character(te$actionID_f), colnames(p))
    pr <- ifelse(is.na(idx), 1e-6, p[cbind(seq_len(nrow(te)), ifelse(is.na(idx), 1, idx))])
    log(pmax(pr, 1e-9))
  })
  if (any(map_lgl(per_row, ~ anyNA(.x)))) return(NA_real_)
  mean(unlist(per_row))
}

treatment_diag$cv_gain <- NA_real_
treatment_diag$used <- FALSE
treatments_used <- character(0)
combined_gain <- NA_real_

if (can_fit_model && length(eligible) > 0 && n_sess >= 4) {
  cv_cols <- c(predictor_cols_base, eligible)
  cv_cols <- varying_cols(model_data, cv_cols)
  eligible <- intersect(eligible, cv_cols)
  cv_data <- model_data[complete.cases(model_data[, c("actionID_f", cv_cols)]), ]
  K <- min(cv_folds, n_distinct(cv_data$session_id))
  set.seed(1)
  fold_of_session <- setNames(sample(rep(seq_len(K), length.out = n_distinct(cv_data$session_id))),
                              unique(cv_data$session_id))
  folds <- unname(fold_of_session[cv_data$session_id])

  ll_base <- cv_ll(intersect(predictor_cols_base, cv_cols), cv_data, folds)
  cat("held-out mean log-likelihood per decision, state-only model:", round(ll_base, 4), "\n")
  if (!is.na(ll_base)) {
    for (v in eligible) {
      ll_v <- cv_ll(c(intersect(predictor_cols_base, cv_cols), v), cv_data, folds)
      treatment_diag$cv_gain[treatment_diag$variable == v] <- ll_v - ll_base
    }
    treatments_used <- treatment_diag %>%
      filter(variable %in% eligible, !is.na(cv_gain), cv_gain > cv_min_gain) %>% pull(variable)
    if (length(treatments_used) > 0) {
      combined_gain <- cv_ll(c(intersect(predictor_cols_base, cv_cols), treatments_used), cv_data, folds) - ll_base
      if (is.na(combined_gain) || combined_gain <= cv_min_gain) {
        message("Treatments individually helped but not together (combined held-out gain ",
                round(combined_gain, 4), ") -- none used.")
        treatments_used <- character(0)
      }
    }
  }
} else if (length(eligible) > 0) {
  message("Too few sessions (", n_sess, ") for session-blocked cross-validation -- no treatment is used.")
}

treatment_diag <- treatment_diag %>%
  mutate(used = variable %in% treatments_used,
         overall = case_when(
           used ~ "USED as predictor",
           variation_verdict == "not testable" ~ "not used: not testable with this pool",
           is.na(cv_gain) ~ "not used: no cross-validation possible",
           TRUE ~ "not used: no held-out improvement"))

if (length(treatments_used) > 0) {
  predictor_cols <- c(predictor_cols_base, treatments_used)
  predictor_terms <- paste0("`", predictor_cols, "`")
  form <- make_form(predictor_cols)
}
cat("Treatments used as predictors:", if (length(treatments_used) == 0) "(none)" else paste(treatments_used, collapse = ", "), "\n")

if (nrow(treatment_diag) > 0) write_csv(treatment_diag, "treatment_report.csv")
treatment_diag
```

## Step 6: a single pooled model, as a baseline

Useful as a sanity check and a point of comparison against the
per-player/per-class versions below -- if the pooled and per-class
models end up looking nearly identical, that's itself informative (not
much heterogeneity to find, at least not yet, with this much data).

```{r fit-pooled}
if (can_fit_model) {
  fit <- fit_mn(predictor_cols, model_data)
  summary(fit)
}
```

```{r plot-coefs}
if (exists("fit")) {
  coefs <- as.data.frame(coef(fit))
  coefs$outcome_level <- rownames(coefs)
  coefs_long <- coefs %>% pivot_longer(-outcome_level, names_to = "term", values_to = "weight")

  ggplot(coefs_long, aes(x = term, y = weight, fill = outcome_level)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Pooled model: fitted feature weights per action",
         x = NULL, y = "coefficient (log-odds scale, relative to the reference action)") +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

## Step 6b: which patch? (the patch-choice model)

The action model above answers "given that I am on this patch, what do I do?"
It cannot see WHERE a person chooses to act, because patches they did not
touch are not in the data. This step adds that missing half. A turn is a
sequence of picks: at each pick the player chooses one patch from those that
could still be acted on (the logged `landChoices` says which), or chooses to
**stop**. A conditional logit estimates how patch features (soil quality,
distance to water, whether it is a protected area, whether the crop is yours,
which actions are available there, ...) raise or lower the chance a patch is
picked next, and how likely stopping is as picks accumulate. The same patch
variables as the action model are used; nothing game-specific is added.

Patches picked are those a player's last tap left with an action (a patch
tapped and cycled back to "do nothing" is browsing, not a pick). Pick order is
the order of first taps. When more than `choice_max_alternatives` patches are
eligible, the unchosen ones are a random sample; that is unbiased for this
model, so no correction is needed. Weights are shown per standard deviation of
each feature in the guide, and per raw unit in `agent_patch_choice_weights.csv`.

```{r patch-choice-data}
patch_choice_ok <- FALSE
pc <- NULL
pc_fit <- NULL            # pc plus any treatment terms accepted in Step 6c
pc_note <- "patch-choice model not run"

fit_choice <- function(pc, S = NULL, ridge = choice_ridge, iters = 60) {
  if (is.null(S)) S <- seq_len(pc$E)
  A <- pc$A; E <- length(S)
  rows <- rep((S - 1L) * A, each = A) + seq_len(A)
  Xs <- pc$Xs[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  V  <- matrix(pc$valid[rows], nrow = E, ncol = A, byrow = TRUE)
  ch <- pc$CH[S]
  d <- ncol(Xs); grp <- rep(seq_len(E), each = A)
  xs <- Xs[(seq_len(E) - 1L) * A + ch, , drop = FALSE]
  probs <- function(b) {
    u <- matrix(as.vector(Xs %*% b), nrow = E, ncol = A, byrow = TRUE)
    u[!V] <- -Inf
    e <- exp(u - apply(u, 1, max))
    e / rowSums(e)
  }
  objective <- function(b) {
    p <- probs(b)
    -sum(log(pmax(p[cbind(seq_len(E), ch)], 1e-300))) + ridge * sum(b^2)
  }
  b <- rep(0, d); f0 <- objective(b)
  for (it in seq_len(iters)) {
    p <- probs(b); pv <- as.vector(t(p))
    xbar <- rowsum(Xs * pv, grp, reorder = FALSE)
    g <- -colSums(xs - xbar) + 2 * ridge * b
    Xw <- Xs * sqrt(pv)
    H <- crossprod(Xw) - crossprod(xbar) + 2 * ridge * diag(d)
    step <- tryCatch(solve(H + 1e-8 * diag(d), g), error = function(e) g / (max(abs(diag(H))) + 1))
    tt <- 1; f1 <- f0
    while (tt > 1e-6) {
      f1 <- objective(b - tt * step)
      if (is.finite(f1) && f1 <= f0) break
      tt <- tt / 2
    }
    if (!(is.finite(f1) && f1 <= f0)) break
    b <- b - tt * step
    done <- abs(f0 - f1) < 1e-7 * max(1, abs(f0))
    f0 <- f1
    if (done) break
  }
  list(beta_std = b, beta_raw = b / pc$sdv,
       mean_loglik = -(f0 - ridge * sum(b^2)) / E,
       mean_loglik_uniform = -mean(log(rowSums(V))), n_events = E)
}

if (use_patch_choice && can_fit_model && "landChoices" %in% names(state_wide)) {
  pc_note <- tryCatch({
    action_ids <- sort(setdiff(unique(choice_real$actionID), -99))
    own_vars <- intersect(unique(variable_roles$variable[variable_roles$role %in% c("ownership_individual", "player_reference")]), names(state_wide))

    lc <- state_wide$landChoices
    n_opts <- lengths(str_extract_all(ifelse(is.na(lc), "", lc), "-?[0-9]+")) - 1
    PF <- state_wide[!is.na(lc) & n_opts > 0, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(PF) == 0) stop("no patch has any available action in landChoices")

    player_level <- c("currentScore", "totalScore", "resources", "n_taps_patch", "n_taps_turn")
    counters_in <- c(counter_included, paste0(counter_included, c("_sin", "_cos")))
    A_cols <- setdiff(intersect(predictor_cols_base, names(PF)), c(player_level, own_vars, counters_in))
    feat_df <- PF[, A_cols, drop = FALSE] %>% mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.numeric))
    feat_df <- feat_df[, !map_lgl(feat_df, ~ is.factor(.x) && nlevels(droplevels(.x)) < 2), drop = FALSE]
    mm <- if (ncol(feat_df) > 0) model.matrix(~ ., data = feat_df, na.action = na.pass)[, -1, drop = FALSE] else matrix(0, nrow(PF), 0)
    mm[is.na(mm)] <- 0
    avail <- sapply(action_ids, function(a) as.numeric(str_detect(PF$landChoices, paste0("(^|[^0-9-])", a, "($|[^0-9])"))))
    avail <- matrix(avail, nrow = nrow(PF)); colnames(avail) <- paste0("avail_", action_ids)
    PFmat <- cbind(mm, avail)
    if (length(own_vars) > 0) {
      OWN <- matrix(sapply(own_vars, function(v) as.numeric(as.character(PF[[v]]))), nrow = nrow(PF))
      colnames(OWN) <- own_vars
    } else OWN <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(PF), 0)

    PF_key   <- paste(PF$session_id, PF$round, PF$phase, PF$x, PF$y, sep = "|")
    elig_by_phase <- split(seq_len(nrow(PF)), paste(PF$session_id, PF$round, PF$phase, sep = "|"))

    # every tap in file order -> the patches each player picked in each turn, in order of first tap
    tp <- choice %>% mutate(tap_i = row_number()) %>%
      group_by(session_id, round, phase, player, x, y) %>%
      summarise(first_i = min(tap_i), final = actionID[which.max(tap_i)], .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(final != -99) %>% arrange(first_i)
    picks_by_turn <- split(paste(tp$session_id, tp$round, tp$phase, tp$x, tp$y, sep = "|"),
                           paste(tp$session_id, tp$round, tp$phase, tp$player))

    turns <- bind_rows(
      confirm %>% transmute(session_id, round = as.numeric(round), phase = as.numeric(phase), player = as.numeric(player)),
      choice %>% distinct(session_id, round, phase, player)) %>%
      distinct() %>% left_join(person_map, by = c("session_id", "player")) %>%
      arrange(session_id, round, phase, player)
    turn_keys  <- paste(turns$session_id, turns$round, turns$phase, turns$player)
    phase_keys <- paste(turns$session_id, turns$round, turns$phase, sep = "|")

    A_max <- choice_max_alternatives
    n_alloc <- nrow(tp) + nrow(turns)
    ALT <- matrix(0L, nrow = n_alloc, ncol = A_max)
    CH <- integer(n_alloc); EVP <- numeric(n_alloc); EVK <- numeric(n_alloc)
    EV_person <- character(n_alloc); EV_session <- character(n_alloc)
    STOP_ROW <- nrow(PF) + 1L
    ne <- 0L
    set.seed(1)
    for (ti in seq_len(nrow(turns))) {
      el <- elig_by_phase[[phase_keys[ti]]]
      if (is.null(el)) next
      pk <- picks_by_turn[[turn_keys[ti]]]
      pick_rows <- if (is.null(pk)) integer(0) else match(pk, PF_key)
      pick_rows <- pick_rows[!is.na(pick_rows)]
      remaining <- el
      seq_ev <- c(pick_rows, STOP_ROW)
      for (k in seq_along(seq_ev)) {
        chn <- seq_ev[k]
        others <- setdiff(remaining, chn)
        if (length(others) > A_max - 2) others <- others[sample.int(length(others), A_max - 2)]
        alts <- if (chn == STOP_ROW) c(others, STOP_ROW) else c(others, chn, STOP_ROW)
        ne <- ne + 1L
        ALT[ne, seq_along(alts)] <- alts
        CH[ne] <- if (chn == STOP_ROW) length(alts) else length(others) + 1L
        EVP[ne] <- turns$player[ti]; EVK[ne] <- k - 1; EV_person[ne] <- turns$person_id[ti]; EV_session[ne] <- turns$session_id[ti]
        if (chn != STOP_ROW) remaining <- setdiff(remaining, chn)
      }
    }
    if (ne < 100) stop(sprintf("only %d choice events", ne))
    ALT <- ALT[seq_len(ne), , drop = FALSE]
    CH <- CH[seq_len(ne)]; EVP <- EVP[seq_len(ne)]; EVK <- EVK[seq_len(ne)]
    EV_person <- EV_person[seq_len(ne)]; EV_session <- EV_session[seq_len(ne)]

    # design matrix, event-major: rows (e-1)*A+1 ... e*A are event e's alternatives
    PFfull  <- rbind(PFmat, 0)
    OWNfull <- if (ncol(OWN) > 0) rbind(OWN, NA_real_) else OWN
    idx <- as.vector(t(ALT))
    valid <- idx != 0L
    rows_i <- ifelse(valid, idx, STOP_ROW)
    Xb <- PFfull[rows_i, , drop = FALSE]
    if (ncol(OWN) > 0) {
      mine <- OWNfull[rows_i, , drop = FALSE] == rep(EVP, each = A_max)
      mine[is.na(mine)] <- FALSE
      mine <- matrix(as.numeric(mine), nrow = length(idx)); colnames(mine) <- paste0(own_vars, "_mine")
    } else mine <- matrix(0, nrow = length(idx), ncol = 0)
    is_stop <- as.numeric(idx == STOP_ROW)
    X <- cbind(Xb, mine, stop = is_stop, stop_k = is_stop * rep(EVK, each = A_max))
    sdv <- apply(X[valid, , drop = FALSE], 2, sd)
    keepc <- !is.na(sdv) & sdv > 1e-9
    X <- X[, keepc, drop = FALSE]; sdv <- sdv[keepc]
    Xs <- sweep(X, 2, sdv, "/")
    Xs[!valid, ] <- 0

    pc <- list(Xs = Xs, valid = valid, CH = CH, E = ne, A = A_max, EVP = EVP, EV_person = EV_person,
               EV_session = EV_session, colnames = colnames(X), sdv = sdv)
    pooled_choice_fit <- fit_choice(pc)
    patch_choice_ok <- TRUE
    sprintf("%d picks/stops from %d turns; %d patch-choice features; pooled mean log-likelihood per pick %.2f vs %.2f for choosing uniformly",
            ne, nrow(turns), ncol(X), pooled_choice_fit$mean_loglik, pooled_choice_fit$mean_loglik_uniform)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Patch-choice model skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))
    paste("patch-choice model skipped:", conditionMessage(e))
  })
} else if (use_patch_choice) {
  pc_note <- "patch-choice model skipped: the logs have no landChoices (log them with tapSquares v3 or later)"
  message(pc_note)
}
cat(pc_note, "\n")
if (patch_choice_ok) {
  print(tibble(feature = pc$colnames, weight_per_sd = round(pooled_choice_fit$beta_std, 2)), n = Inf)
}
```

## Step 6c: do treatments change which patches get picked?

A session-wide setting such as the fine probability is the same for every
patch in a choice, so on its own it cannot change which patch is picked: it
raises or lowers all patches together and cancels. What it CAN change is how
attractive some kinds of patch are (for example, protected land when fines are
high), or how soon people stop. Those are **interactions**: the treatment
crossed with a patch feature (or with the "stop" option). There are many
possible crossings, so they are screened first and then validated:

1. **Screen.** With the patch-choice model fitted WITHOUT treatments, look at what
   it gets wrong in each session (how far the picks fall from the model's
   expectation for each feature). If a treatment crossed with a feature
   matters, those session-level errors will line up with the treatment across
   sessions. A t-statistic across sessions (so a few sessions cannot masquerade
   as thousands of independent picks) ranks every crossing in one pass,
   without refitting.
2. **Validate.** The best few crossings per treatment are added to the model and
   tested by cross-validation on whole sessions, like Step 5a. A treatment's
   crossings are used only if they improve the prediction of picks in sessions
   the model was not fitted on.

```{r patch-choice-treatments}
choice_treatment_table <- NULL
choice_treatment_note <- "patch-choice treatments not examined"
choice_used_treatments <- character(0)
pc_fit <- pc

choice_loglik <- function(b, pc, S) {
  A <- pc$A; E <- length(S)
  rows <- rep((S - 1L) * A, each = A) + seq_len(A)
  u <- matrix(as.vector(pc$Xs[rows, , drop = FALSE] %*% b), nrow = E, ncol = A, byrow = TRUE)
  V <- matrix(pc$valid[rows], nrow = E, ncol = A, byrow = TRUE)
  u[!V] <- -Inf
  m <- apply(u, 1, max)
  u[cbind(seq_len(E), pc$CH[S])] - (m + log(rowSums(exp(u - m))))
}

choice_residual_matrix <- function(pc, b) {
  E <- pc$E; A <- pc$A
  u <- matrix(as.vector(pc$Xs %*% b), nrow = E, ncol = A, byrow = TRUE)
  u[!matrix(pc$valid, nrow = E, ncol = A, byrow = TRUE)] <- -Inf
  e <- exp(u - apply(u, 1, max)); p <- e / rowSums(e)
  xbar <- rowsum(pc$Xs * as.vector(t(p)), rep(seq_len(E), each = A), reorder = FALSE)
  pc$Xs[(seq_len(E) - 1L) * A + pc$CH, , drop = FALSE] - xbar
}

# the patch-choice design with extra columns: each term is (treatment x design column)
add_choice_terms <- function(pc, terms) {
  if (nrow(terms) == 0) return(pc)
  newcols <- list(); inter <- list(); nm <- character(0); sdv_new <- numeric(0)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(terms))) {
    tv <- as.numeric(session_params[[terms$treat[i]]][match(pc$EV_session, session_params$session_id)])
    m <- mean(tv); sdt <- sd(tv)
    fcol <- match(terms$feat[i], pc$colnames)
    newcols[[i]] <- rep((tv - m) / sdt, each = pc$A) * pc$Xs[, fcol]
    nm <- c(nm, paste0(terms$treat[i], ":", terms$feat[i]))
    sdv_new <- c(sdv_new, pc$sdv[fcol] * sdt)
    inter[[i]] <- tibble(feat_col = fcol, t_mean = m)
  }
  out <- pc
  out$inter <- bind_rows(inter) %>% mutate(col = ncol(pc$Xs) + row_number(), treat = terms$treat, feat = terms$feat)
  out$Xs <- cbind(pc$Xs, do.call(cbind, newcols))
  out$colnames <- c(pc$colnames, nm)
  out$sdv <- c(pc$sdv, sdv_new)
  out
}

# weights on the ORIGINAL scale: for each feature value x and treatment value t,
#   sum of  weight * x  +  weight_interaction * (t * x)
choice_raw <- function(beta_std, pcx) {
  raw <- beta_std / pcx$sdv
  if (!is.null(pcx$inter)) for (j in seq_len(nrow(pcx$inter))) {
    raw[pcx$inter$feat_col[j]] <- raw[pcx$inter$feat_col[j]] - raw[pcx$inter$col[j]] * pcx$inter$t_mean[j]
  }
  raw
}

cv_choice <- function(pcx, cols, S_all, fold_of_event) {
  pcs <- pcx; pcs$Xs <- pcx$Xs[, cols, drop = FALSE]; pcs$sdv <- pcx$sdv[cols]
  ll <- numeric(0)
  for (k in sort(unique(fold_of_event))) {
    f <- fit_choice(pcs, S_all[fold_of_event != k], iters = 25)
    ll <- c(ll, choice_loglik(f$beta_std, pcs, S_all[fold_of_event == k]))
  }
  mean(ll)
}

if (use_choice_treatments && patch_choice_ok && exists("treatment_diag") && nrow(treatment_diag) > 0) {
  choice_treatment_note <- tryCatch({
    cand_t <- treatment_diag %>%
      filter(variation_verdict != "not testable", abm_evaluable, type %in% c("numeric", "logical")) %>% pull(variable)
    sess <- sort(unique(pc$EV_session))
    if (length(cand_t) == 0) stop("no treatment varies enough across sessions")
    if (length(sess) < 4) stop("fewer than 4 sessions")

    # ---- 1. screen ----
    R <- choice_residual_matrix(pc, pooled_choice_fit$beta_std)
    Rs <- rowsum(R, pc$EV_session)
    ns <- as.vector(rowsum(rep(1, pc$E), pc$EV_session))
    Rbar <- Rs / ns
    scr <- bind_rows(lapply(cand_t, function(tn) {
      tvs <- as.numeric(session_params[[tn]][match(rownames(Rs), session_params$session_id)])
      r <- suppressWarnings(as.vector(cor(tvs, Rbar)))
      r[is.na(r)] <- 0
      tibble(treat = tn, feat = pc$colnames, t_stat = r * sqrt((length(tvs) - 2) / pmax(1 - r^2, 1e-9)))
    })) %>% arrange(desc(abs(t_stat)))
    top <- scr %>% filter(abs(t_stat) >= choice_screen_min_t) %>% slice_head(n = choice_screen_top)
    scr$screened <- paste(scr$treat, scr$feat) %in% paste(top$treat, top$feat)
    scr$cv_gain <- NA_real_; scr$used <- FALSE
    if (nrow(top) == 0) { choice_treatment_table <<- scr; stop("no treatment x patch-feature crossing showed a session-level association") }

    # ---- 2. validate by cross-validation on whole sessions ----
    set.seed(1)
    S_cv <- if (pc$E > choice_cv_max_events) sort(sample.int(pc$E, choice_cv_max_events)) else seq_len(pc$E)
    K <- min(cv_folds, length(sess))
    fold_of_session <- setNames(sample(rep(seq_len(K), length.out = length(sess))), sess)
    fold_ev <- unname(fold_of_session[pc$EV_session[S_cv]])
    pc_all <- add_choice_terms(pc, top)
    base_cols <- seq_len(ncol(pc$Xs))
    ll_base <- cv_choice(pc_all, base_cols, S_cv, fold_ev)
    cat("patch-choice held-out mean log-likelihood per pick, no treatment terms:", round(ll_base, 4), "\n")
    for (tn in unique(top$treat)) {
      add_cols <- ncol(pc$Xs) + which(top$treat == tn)
      g <- cv_choice(pc_all, c(base_cols, add_cols), S_cv, fold_ev) - ll_base
      scr$cv_gain[scr$treat == tn & scr$screened] <- g
      cat("  + ", tn, " (", length(add_cols), " crossing(s)): gain ", sprintf("%+.4f", g), "\n", sep = "")
    }
    keep_t <- unique(scr$treat[scr$screened & !is.na(scr$cv_gain) & scr$cv_gain > cv_min_gain])
    acc <- top %>% filter(treat %in% keep_t)
    if (nrow(acc) > 0) {
      add_cols <- ncol(pc$Xs) + which(top$treat %in% keep_t)
      comb <- cv_choice(pc_all, c(base_cols, add_cols), S_cv, fold_ev) - ll_base
      if (is.na(comb) || comb <= cv_min_gain) { message("Treatment crossings helped individually but not together -- none used."); acc <- acc[0, ] }
    }
    scr$used <- paste(scr$treat, scr$feat) %in% paste(acc$treat, acc$feat)
    choice_treatment_table <<- scr
    if (nrow(acc) > 0) {
      choice_used_treatments <<- unique(acc$treat)
      pc_fit <<- add_choice_terms(pc, acc)
      pooled_choice_fit <<- fit_choice(pc_fit)
      sprintf("treatment crossings used in patch choice: %s", paste(paste0(acc$treat, ":", acc$feat), collapse = ", "))
    } else "no treatment crossing improved the prediction of picks in held-out sessions"
  }, error = function(e) { message("Patch-choice treatments skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); paste("skipped:", conditionMessage(e)) })
}
cat(choice_treatment_note, "\n")
if (!is.null(choice_treatment_table)) {
  write_csv(choice_treatment_table, "choice_treatment_report.csv")
  print(choice_treatment_table %>% slice_head(n = 15))
}
# A treatment can matter through what people DO on a patch (Step 5a), through WHICH patches they
# go for (this step), or both. Record where, so the ABM hand-off can list every treatment that matters.
if (exists("treatment_diag") && nrow(treatment_diag) > 0) {
  treatment_diag$used_choice <- treatment_diag$variable %in% choice_used_treatments
  treatment_diag$acts_through <- case_when(
    treatment_diag$used & treatment_diag$used_choice ~ "action+patch_choice",
    treatment_diag$used ~ "action",
    treatment_diag$used_choice ~ "patch_choice",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_)
  treatment_diag$overall <- case_when(
    treatment_diag$used & treatment_diag$used_choice ~ "USED: action and patch choice",
    treatment_diag$used_choice ~ "USED: patch choice only",
    TRUE ~ treatment_diag$overall)
  write_csv(treatment_diag, "treatment_report.csv")
}
```

## Step 7: let people differ -- fit one model per person, then cluster

A person is a `person_id`: the string typed at entry, shared across every
session in which it appears. Per-person fits use the state-only formula
(`form_base`) so that classes describe how people respond to the board, not
which treatment sessions they happened to play in; class-level models in
Step 8 then include the treatments that passed Step 5a.

This is a practical two-step *approximation* to a true latent-class
discrete choice model, not the real thing. A proper joint estimator
(e.g. the `gmnl` package's latent-class multinomial logit) fits all
classes simultaneously via EM, sharing information across players in a
statistically principled way. That needs a data format (`mlogit`-style
long-by-alternative, via `dfidx`) that's easy to get subtly wrong
without being able to test it live, and with only a few players from
one session there often isn't yet enough data to make a joint
estimator worth the risk. This fit-per-player-then-cluster version
reuses only the already-validated `multinom()` machinery, so it's far
more likely to actually run -- worth upgrading to `gmnl` once there
are enough sessions/players for a joint estimate to be meaningfully
more powerful than this approximation.

**With only a handful of players, treat this whole step as a
mechanics check, not a real result** until there's enough data to say
otherwise.

```{r fit-per-player}
fit_one_player <- function(pid) {
  player_data <- model_data %>% filter(person_id == pid)
  if (nrow(player_data) < min_decisions_per_person) {
    message("Person ", pid, ": only ", nrow(player_data), " decisions (< ", min_decisions_per_person, ") -- skipping.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  if (n_distinct(player_data$actionID) < 2) {
    message("Person ", pid, ": only one action type observed -- skipping.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  tryCatch(
    fit_mn(predictor_cols_base, player_data),
    error = function(e) {
      message("Person ", pid, ": model failed to fit (", conditionMessage(e), ")")
      NULL
    }
  )
}

if (can_fit_model) {
  player_ids <- sort(unique(model_data$person_id))
  player_fits <- set_names(map(player_ids, fit_one_player), player_ids)
  player_fits <- compact(player_fits)
  cat("Per-person models fit successfully for", length(player_fits), "person(s).\n")
}
```

```{r fit-choice-per-person}
# Patch-choice model, one per person: how does each person pick patches (and when do they stop)?
pc_person_fits <- list()
choice_fingerprint <- NULL
if (patch_choice_ok) {
  big <- which(rowSums(matrix(pc$valid, nrow = pc$E, ncol = pc$A, byrow = TRUE)) >= min(25, pc$A - 1))
  set.seed(2)
  scenes <- if (length(big) > choice_scenes) sample(big, choice_scenes) else big
  scene_rows <- rep((scenes - 1L) * pc$A, each = pc$A) + seq_len(pc$A)
  Xsc <- pc$Xs[scene_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  Vsc <- matrix(pc$valid[scene_rows], nrow = length(scenes), ncol = pc$A, byrow = TRUE)
  # A person's fingerprint: the probability their model gives to each alternative in each of
  # the same common scenes. People who would pick alike in the same circumstances look alike.
  choice_fingerprint <- function(b) {
    u <- matrix(as.vector(Xsc %*% b), nrow = length(scenes), ncol = pc$A, byrow = TRUE)
    u[!Vsc] <- -Inf
    e <- exp(u - apply(u, 1, max))
    as.vector(e / rowSums(e))
  }
  for (pid in sort(unique(pc$EV_person))) {
    S <- which(pc$EV_person == pid)
    if (length(S) < min_choice_events_per_person) {
      message("Person ", pid, ": only ", length(S), " picks (< ", min_choice_events_per_person, ") -- no patch-choice fit.")
      next
    }
    pc_person_fits[[pid]] <- tryCatch(fit_choice(pc, S), error = function(e) {
      message("Person ", pid, ": patch-choice fit failed (", conditionMessage(e), ")"); NULL })
  }
  pc_person_fits <- compact(pc_person_fits)
  cat("Patch-choice models fit for", length(pc_person_fits), "person(s).\n")
}
```
